projection.rationale: Revenue dips sequentially from Q4FY26 peak due to seasonal rental softness, but improves YoY on stable occupancy. OPM holds near 38% on cost control, PAT positive on lower base.
Revenue recovers toward FY26 average; OPM improves to ~40% on operating leverage. PAT includes other income from disinvestment proceeds deployment.

deepdive.sec: Premium Retail Mall Operator & Mixed-Use Developer (MMR Focus)

bull_bear.body: 100% of Rs 1,242.5 Cr from strategic sale of two malls to be redeployed into premium MMR residential/retail projects; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt reduction not prioritized over growth capex
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delays in MMR land acquisition; regulatory approvals for Nagpur Mall; execution risk in residential handovers; LTCG tax impact (12.5% without indexation) on asset sales; reliance on single strategic pivot for future growth
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Despite high occupancy, retail revenue growth is primarily from leasing, not sales; the company is effectively transitioning from a mall operator to a real estate development fund using asset sales as a capital recycling engine
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital allocation philosophy centers on recycling capital from mature, peak-performing assets into higher-growth, premium-location developments, as evidenced by the INR 1,242.5 Cr mall divestment.
- The company generated significant cash from the strategic sale, with stated intent to reinvest net proceeds into high-yield MMR projects rather than returning capital to shareholders.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Retail: Ch Sambhaji Nagar Mall (94% occupancy, 127 stores, Rs 1,303 mn lease income FY26); Coimbatore Mall (96% occupancy, 113 stores, Rs 1,303 mn lease income FY26). Residential: Coimbatore (540 units, 87+ handed over), Nagpur (336 units, 209 handed over), Indore (Phase 1A: 74 plots completed, Phase 1B: 75 plots under sales)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Strategic pivot to MMR: Monetizing peak-performing Tier-2 malls to redeploy capital into high-value, high-growth Grade A office and retail platforms in prime Mumbai CBD locations.
- The deck frames the INR 1,242.5 Cr mall sale as unlocking capital for 'High-Yield Frontiers', leveraging Mumbai's infrastructure boom for superior realty potential.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: - [PAT Turnaround] FY26 PAT turned positive to Rs 178.9 mn from a loss of Rs 543.6 mn in FY25, driven by operational improvements and a one-time deferred tax remeasurement impact from the revised LTCG tax rate.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin: 48.1% (FY26), up from 32.2% (FY25); EBITDA excluding other income margin: 39.3% (FY26); cost control driven by high occupancy and rental stability; no material cost inflation cited
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Strategic pivot toward high-yield MMR developments using proceeds from strategic disinvestment of Ch Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore malls; targeting premium residential and retail projects in Mumbai CBD.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Coimbatore Residential: 402/540 units sold (Rs 2,167 mn); Nagpur Residential: 254/336 units sold (Rs 1,780 mn); Indore Phase 1B: 54/75 plots under EOI
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Nagpur Mall (0.5m sqft retail + 0.39m sqft development potential); Indore township (43.5 acres, Phase 2+); MMR CBD land acquisition using Rs 1,242.5 Cr disinvestment proceeds
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Prozone Realty is strategically monetizing high-performing retail assets in Tier-II cities to redeploy capital into premium Grade-A residential and retail projects in Mumbai's CBD, leveraging peak occupancy and strong footfall to unlock value. The shift from asset-heavy operations to capital-efficient development positions it for margin expansion and higher ROCE in India's most resilient real estate market.
